column1: # Which clauses can carry a scenario, and which cannot.
# tests/spec/run.py reads this to turn a clause-coverage *report* into a gate
# (ADR-0106). Without it the denominator is every heading in both standards,
# and most of them -- containers, definitions, the standard's own examples --
# could never carry a scenario, so the percentage was one nobody could act on.
# That is the mistake ADR-0104 avoided in rejecting block coverage, met again
# Three classes, and the gate treats them differently:
#   testable          states a requirement a Pascal program can exercise, and
#                     this processor implements it. Cited by a scenario or not
#                     yet; the count of "not yet" is a ratchet.
#   structural        cannot carry a scenario. A citation of one FAILS -- either
#                     the triage is wrong or the scenario is tagged with the
#                     wrong clause, and both are worth hearing about.
#   not-implemented   this processor does not provide the feature, by a
#                     documented decision. A citation FAILS for the same reason.
#                     Two kinds of decision land here and the class does not
#                     distinguish them, because the gate's answer is the same:
#                     a feature declined, and a feature specified ahead of the
#                     processor (AP 5.6). What the class buys in the second
#                     case is that the specification cannot come to claim,
#                     through a passing scenario, that the feature is there.
#                     There are none of either kind at present. AP 6.4.15 held
#                     every row of this class for three days and was taken off
#                     a clause at a time as it was built (ADR-0190 - ADR-0192),
#                     which is the class working rather than the class going
# So the gate is two-directional, as tests/checks/uncovered_procedures.txt is:
# a clause that stops being cited fails, and a clause that starts being cited
# and should not be fails too.
# The triage is a *reading*, and nothing here can check a reading -- which is
# the whole reason tests/spec/ exists. Argue a change in the commit message.
